plan.title: Live Nov 6: asked agreement to a step the tester never saw

context.text: Hey! It's 6:40, so the Alex draft is up. Two lines is plenty. Send me a screenshot when it's written, and don't send it to him yet.

transcript.text: [photo alex-draft.jpg: an unsent Notes draft to Alex asking for 10 minutes, no pitch]

Day 4 done, Yanni! 🔥 "No pitch, promise" is a great line, because it makes the ask easy to say yes to. You said yesterday that reaching out feels a little intimidating. How did it feel to write a message to a real person this time?
Awkward makes sense, since it's a real person and not just a list. What part felt the most awkward: asking for his time, or the idea of him reading it?
Asking for his time. I worry it’ll feel like I’m bothering him
Totally normal worry, Yanni. Asking for someone's time is the part most people hate. When you picture Alex reading it, what do you imagine him thinking?

conversation.reason: After the draft photo, ZOH opened the reflection with one question about how writing it felt, and didn't chase it later.
Each follow-up builds on what the tester said, with one question per text and no list.
'A little awkward' got a proof-grounded follow-up asking what part felt awkward, with no guess at its meaning.
The worry about bothering Alex got a question about what he might think before any step; a short reassurance comes first.
ZOH went deeper on the bothering worry with a question, and proposed no next step or agreement request.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the reflection well: it asked one question after the draft, followed the tester's 'awkward' and worry about bothering Alex, and kept each text short with one question. It avoided the regression by staying on the worry and not proposing a step or asking for agreement.
